name: Daratumumab + Lenalidomide + Dexamethasone (DRd)

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: DRd is an antibody-based triplet and is not biomarker-restricted for eligibility. Cytogenetic risk (FISH for t(4;14), t(14;16), t(14;20), del(17p)/TP53, gain/amp 1q) informs risk stratification (R-ISS/R2-ISS), not access to DRd. Type and screen must be performed before starting daratumumab because the antibody interferes with serologic (indirect antiglobulin) testing. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Multiple Myeloma, v5.2026.

treatmentSetting: primary therapy for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma when hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) is deferred or not indicated (transplant-ineligible)

premedications.name: Daratumumab infusion/injection-reaction prophylaxis
premedications.notes: corticosteroid, antihistamine and antipyretic before daratumumab; montelukast may be added for reaction risk per institutional practice.

supportiveCare: Daratumumab: monitor for infusion/injection reactions (mainly with the first dose); perform type and screen before the first dose (serologic interference).
Lenalidomide: VTE thromboprophylaxis (aspirin for standard risk, therapeutic anticoagulation for higher risk) and REMS-program dispensing (teratogen); adjust for renal impairment.
Herpes zoster (VZV) and Pneumocystis prophylaxis per institutional practice (anti-CD38 antibody infection risk).
Antiemetics: low emetic risk; prophylaxis per emetogenicity tier.
monitoring: CBC with differential and platelets before each cycle
renal function and electrolytes (lenalidomide renal clearance)

doseModificationRules.text: Hold and resume lenalidomide at a reduced dose per labeling for grade 3 to 4 cytopenia; clinical review.

drugs.name: Daratumumab
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., Table 74.6, p.1520 (line 286349). Daratumumab 1,800 mg SC (or 16 mg/kg IV) weekly for 8 weeks, then every 2 weeks for 4 months, then once monthly, continued until progression. On a 28-day cycle the weekly induction maps to days 1, 8, 15, 22 (cycles 1 to 2); the every-2-weeks phase to days 1 and 15 (approximately cycles 3 to 6); the monthly phase to day 1. Give infusion/injection-reaction premedication (corticosteroid, antihistamine, antipyretic). Perform type and screen before the first dose (interferes with indirect antiglobulin testing).

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: Chapter 74, Table 74.6 (Common Treatment Regimens in Multiple Myeloma), p.1520, DRd entry, line 286349 (Daratumumab 1,800 mg SC (or 16 mg/kg IV) weekly x 8 weeks and then every 2 weeks for 4 months, and then once monthly)

drugs.name: Lenalidomide
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., Table 74.6, p.1520 (line 286351). Lenalidomide 25 mg PO on days 1 to 21 of a 28-day cycle. Requires VTE thromboprophylaxis (aspirin or anticoagulation) and REMS-program dispensing (teratogen); reduce dose for renal impairment per CrCl.

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: Chapter 74, Table 74.6, p.1520, DRd entry, line 286351 (Lenalidomide 25 mg PO on days 1-21)

drugs.name: Dexamethasone
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., Table 74.6, p.1520 (line 286352). Dexamethasone 40 mg PO on days 1, 8, 15, and 22 of a 28-day cycle. A lower dose may be used for older or frail patients; dose taken exactly as the source prints it.
